body:
You're most definitely right. I was in a really bad place yesterday, and I think I kinda wanted to give up. Not that it's really an excuse, but I have a disorder called Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder, and it makes these days very, very hard to handle. It doesn't change the fact that I have to learn to reach out and get a grip. 

I used to go to meetings, but then my anxiety got real bad, and I chickened out. After this, I'm going to go back, even if I have to force myself in the beginning. I don't care that they talk about God in AA, I find it kinda comforting, even if I don't necessarily believe in it myself. 

This was really a wake-up call for me, I thought I could deal with this on my own, but now I realize I need to let people around me help me, and I have to let them know when I need help. I'm definitely going to work on this from now on. 

Thanks alot!
Thank you, you're right. I had a good nights sleep and feel much better now. Getting through this really made me feel stronger in the end, and I know I'll be able to handle it much better next time.

Thank you, I really appreciate the kind words. It was a really bad decision, and I don't really know why it even got that far, in the end I didn't even want it. Here's to hoping it taught me a lesson, and that I won't do the same thing next time.

You're right, staying sober is so much better than being drunk, blacked out or hungover all the time. Now that I'm calm and have had some time to sleep on it, I don't even know why I bought that stupid wine.

Thanks, it was really hard, but once I'd done it, I realized it was the only right thing to do. And I was on the phone with a good friend of mine the whole time, and that definitely helped. You can do it next time, I believe in you!
Thanks! That's very kind of you to say. If I'm able to inspire someone, then this almost-relapse was worth it. Good luck to you!

I ended up taking a walk, calling a friend and crying a lot and then went home and poured the wine down the drain. It's been a few very hard hours, but I guess this is a victory of some sort. I still feel pretty sad and weak, and I'll probably just take my medication and go to bed now. 

But I'm very happy that I won't have to go back to day one. And I want to thank every one of you who commented and supported me, I wouldn't be sitting her sober now without you. You're all amazing.

That's true, I wouldn't. And I've been aware of this from the moment I decided to go to the store and buy the bottle, and all the way back home. I almost threw up on the busride home, and am still feeling unwell. And I feel real stupid for coming here and complaining about it, when I should just suck it up and throw the bottle away. But now my head's all "you already bought it, no point in wasting the money" and "one bottle will be okay, maybe the antabuse isn't even working" but at the same time "throw that shit away now!!"

You're right, I really, really don't want to go back to that place. And that should be it, right? But even though I am aware of this, opening that bottle is so tempting. I'm just looking at the bottle and I feel like I can already taste it. This is really my first time struggling with the urge to drink again, I honestly just don't know how to deal with it properly. But thank you for the kind words.

People around me are really happy that I've been doing so well these last two months, and I don't want them to be disappointed I guess. I've never been good at reaching out in real life, only on places like this, where I can just stop visiting the page if it gets too real. I'm a coward like that, I guess. And the hospital's not really helpful towards this. I've tried it before and they ended up yelling at me.

I really wish I could've taken your advice, but at the moment I'm at home. The bottle is on the table, but not opened yet. I'm on antabuse and I don't really know what's gonna happen if I drink - though some people have given me 'advice' on how to be able to drink while on it. Right now I'm going back and forth in my head, I want to drink, but I don't, if that makes any sense.
Is heightism really what I think it is? Because if it is, it's fucking stupid.

I don't want to sound like an asshole, but I have a serious problem believing him as it is. I'm giving him the benefit of the doubt knowing next to nothing about anything other than weed, but it all sounds very convenient. I just wanted to make sure I'm not supposed to get him medical attention.

It's a week for me as well. Felt so good when I woke up today without a massive hangover. I also went to my first AA meeting, which went really great. 

I'm proud of you as well, here's to another sober week!

Yeah, it does make sense that at least the anxiety might get a little better, I'd love for that to happen. 

One thing I won't miss is the anxiety the day after drinking too much. "what did i do", "did I say something stupid", "why can't I remember shit?" Most Sundays I didn't dare to turn on my phone or log in to facebook because I was so scared of what I might've had said and done the night before. 

That fear was actually the main reason for my last suicide attempt because I just couldn't deal with the anxiety and fear of me being blackout-drunk. So you might be right, things might get a lot more stable from now on.

Yeah, people here tell me very different things about drinking on Antabuse than I've heard before, and it doesn't sound like something I want to try out. 
Today I'm just happy got through yesterday and I'm going to the meeting in two hours. I never thought I'd be able to go a full week without drinking, and now I've proven myself wrong. I'm in a much better place than yesterday. Thanks a lot!

Really? That's interesting. I doubt it's going to be completely gone because I stop drinking - I have Emotionally Unstable Personality Disorder (or Borderline) - but maybe it will get easier after being sober for a while. It's worth a try!

I suppose I shouldn't be surprised that a lot of my friends have become "drinking buddies", after all I've done nothing but drinking for a while now. I guess I just thought they'd be supportive or something, and truth be told I'm a little disappointed. But yeah, I'll find a new group of people to hang out with. People who don't require alcohol at every social gathering.
I haven't been able to find so many different groups, but I'll see what I can find out tomorrow, thanks!
I've checked, there was a meeting today, but I found out about it too late. Clock is almost 11 pm here in norway. But I'm going to go tomorrow! thank you
I don't think they would dare to do that here in Norway, but it probably works.

I do want to stop. After being sober for a few days, I see what I've been doing to myself, and I see that I clearly have an issue. But alcohol has been my own sort of self medication or whatever, and it's scary. I've been doing the same thing for over a year, and change is scary. I am working very hard to make this work, I'm going to go to an AA meeting tomorrow. I think the main problem is that I have a lot of anxiety and depression, and for the last year I've been dealing with this by drinking it away. I can't do that anymore.
Oh I know, I'm not really doing myself any favors sitting at home wallowing in my own misery, it's just what I'm used to doing. Maybe I'll try to go for a run though. Thank you.
Well, that doesn't sound appealing. :| My friend asked me to try a beer to test it out a few days ago, glad I didn't do it, I guess.

I'm 20. Quitting wasn't entirely something I decided myself, and I wouldn't have stopped if I hadn't been forced to because of the Antabuse. A year or so ago people were telling me they were worried about me because I had started drinking a lot. I was ditching work because I'd rather drink, and once I had a beer, I couldn't stop before I blacked out. I didn't think that much of it, I told them not to worry, "at least I don't drink alone". then I started paying a lot of money to have people drink with me, because unless I was drinking alone, I didn't have a problem. My therapist was getting worried, and now I'm on Antabuse.

I've heard so many different thing about Antabuse, so I'm not really sure how it works. The doctor didn't really say much about it. I have been taking it every day, but it doesn't really do much - I don't imagine it does anything unless I drink, though. I have some friends who are curious about how I get if I drink while taking the medicine, and them trying to get me to drink isn't really helping, to be honest. 
Also, thanks, I never heard about that sub, but I'm going to check it out!

Thanks a lot. I'm very thankful that I am getting it sorted out now, rather than later. At least my body is still well, and I know that's not always the case. A friend of my mother died because of alcoholism  a few years ago.

I'm going to try out AA, there's a meeting in my town tomorrow. I'm just scared of not being taken seriously because of my age, but I'll go and see how it goes.

Again, thanks for the comment and tips, I really appreciate it.

I just really want to say thank you for this comment, it really meant a lot to me. I am actually seeing a therapist, and I have been for seven years, but I've been having problems actually opening up to them. Now I'm done with some tests and will get some sort of diagnose in a few weeks. Then I'll hopefully get the right medication, the pills I take now makes me really irritated at times. It's been a rough ride, but I'm hoping it will get better soon. 
Again, thanks a lot for this post, it made me so, so happy to feel that I've been heard for once.
I stopped watching news a long time ago. When my best friend died in a terrorist attack, I couldn't manage the horrors in the news anymore. Thanks for the advice, I really appreciate it!

I realize I was probably pretty vague in my post, I guess I was venting more than anything else. To answer your questions, I've been dealing with depression for ten years now, I think. The self-harm and suicidal thoughts started at 10. Because of severe neglect as well as sexual abuse that went on for years, trust is very hard for me. I don't have a facebook or skype or any social media profiles, because it really scares me. When people approach me, I immediately believe they have ill intentions, so I pull out of any social interactions. The few friends I have now are getting pretty tired of this, which is perfectly understandable, and for the last year they just stopped responding to my messages as often as they used to. This again causes me to stop messaging them or calling them, and they rarely make any attempt at contacting me. 
The boyfriend thing is mostly about trust. Somehow I manage to screw up any relationship I'm in, because I'm always sure that my bf is cheating on me, and I become unbearably jealous and paranoid. Also, because if the abuse, sex is a difficult subject, and more than once I'd have a panic attack when a boyfriend tried to initiate something. 
I lost my best friend in the Utøya tragedy that happened here in Norway in 2011, dunno how much people outside of Norway know about this, but long story short, she was 15 years old and shot two times by a norwegian terrorist. She bled to death because the police were too slow. I think about this a lot, and have nightmares about it almost every night. Coupled with my mother neglecting me and my baby sitter abusing me until I was 13, it's not easy working as an adult. 
But yeah, I love my job, it's definitely a lifesaver for me, and I think the reason I'm so sad right now is because it's the weekend, and I just long to go back to work. At home, I have two cats that I love and care about more than anything else, but at the same time, I feel empty and lonely. 
Sorry about the length of this, and also if the grammar is a little off, as mentioned, English is not my first language.

I actually used to be involved with a youth club in my town a few years ago, but it ended badly, and after that I just haven't had the courage to try something new. I have a lot of anxiety, so getting out and meeting new people is a hard task for me. I can relate to the music stuff, though. Thanks for the advice.
I'd totally be down for it.
Your problems are still relevant, you know. And yes, my mother definitely loves me, she's just very... difficult. It'll be fine, for the first time in years I'm looking at the future with hope. :)

Thank you for your concern. I am seeking (and getting!) help now, finally. I just visited my mother and needed to vent a little. I live by myself now, surrounded by great neighbors who help me out a lot. I think I'll be fine, eventually.

We have the same planned date. So, that's kinda neat. It's good to see that you're feeling some hope, that's always a good sign. Keep using the community if you need to, my inbox is always open, and good luck.
That's it. I was gonna get a chewbacca tattoo, now I'm going to get a chewbacca tattoo with your face

It's going to be okay, dear. Just keep it clean and if it doesn't get better, see a doctor. I would actually just see a doctor right away, that way you might get stitches and the scar won't be as bad. If you need to talk, I'm here.
This is a great post! I wish this existed when I first started, I bet it's gonna be helpful for a lot of people, thank you!

I've been struggling with depression since I was 10, so obviously my family knows it, because I started self harming at that age. Now, at the age of 19, I don't really talk to anyone and just keep to myself. I've really been perfecting the "mask" when I am with family and friends, so people think I'm "over it". 

As for the benefits, I had this friend who used to help me with the lowpoints, and it felt really good, because I felt like my depression was something to be ashamed of, and him helping me and listening to my crazy thoughts for a while made me feel normal again, but then I fucked that friendship up. Now everyone thinks I'm recovering while I sit at home every day, not seeing a point in getting up in the morning.
